Subject (in full) Re. 'Assassination of General Yang Yung Tai (楊永泰).

Made by... and Forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne

Inspector Hsu Bang Fei (许鹏飛) of the Woosung-Shanghai
Garrison Commander's Headquarters requests that assistance be
rendered in locating the original of the attached photograph,
who is wanted by the Hankow Authorities on a charge of participat-
ing in the murder of General Yang Yung Tai (楊永泰), the Governor
of Hupeh, at Hankow on October 26. This man, Yang Er Chien
(楊尔謙) alias Pah Kwan (伯坤) is a native of Kweichow, age 25
years, and was educated at Chih Ts University, Klangwan. He was
at one time employed with the Special Service Squad of the Peace
Preservation Corps at Shanghai, and after leaving this position
he was engaged in journalistic work. It is known that he was
in Hankow recently and returned to Shanghai immediately after the
assassination of General Yang.
His paramour, Tsang Soo Yuen (    ) or Nyi Sz (倪氏), who
resided with her parents at 34, Lane 381, Weihaiwei Rd., was
formerly employed as a dancing partner at the Ambassador Ballroom.
The wanted man was a nightly visitor to Chinese cabarets and
is known by sight to several members of the Force.

P.A.
Prepare Photo.

D.C. (Special Branch).
D. S. I.

Date November 13 19 36.
Subject The assassination of General Yang Yung Tai, Governor of Hupeh.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne
With reference to the comment of the D.C. (Special Branch)
concerning the political attitude of late General Yang Yung Tai
(楊永泰) it has now been learned that the reason given by those
concerned in his murder was that he was pro-Japanese.
General Yang was the leader of the Politico-Scholastic
Group, an organization well acquainted with Japanese affairs.
The restraining influence of this group did not meet with
the approval of the leftist element of the Blue Shirts - now
known as the Lih Ying Zo(力行社) - many of whom are ex-Whampao
students under the influence of the Kwangsi clique. Believing
that General Yang was responsible for the refusal of the
Generalissimo to take action in North China, this group detail-
ed several of their members to carry out the murder of General
Yang. Chen Shih Chao( ) who was arrested immediately
after the crime was committed, admitted being a member of the
Special Service Squad of the Blue Shirts, and being concerned
with four others of the same organization in the murder.
D.B.R.
13/11.
J. Coyne.
D. S. I.
D. C. (Special Branch)
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH 13 NOV. 1936 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

主题 湖北省主席杨永泰将军遇刺案。
撰写人及转呈人：警司 Coyne

关于特务科副警务总监对已故杨永泰将军 (Yang Yung Tai) 政治态度的评论，现已获悉，涉案人员给出的谋杀理由是杨亲日。
杨将军是政学系的领袖，该组织对日本事务颇为熟悉。该组织的牵制作用未得到蓝衣社左派元素——现称为力行社 (Lih Ying Zo)——的认可，其中许多人是受广西系影响的黄埔军校前学生。该团体认为杨将军应对委员长拒绝在华北采取行动负责，因此指派几名成员执行刺杀杨将军的任务。陈世召 (Chen Shih Chao)( ) 在案发后立即被捕，承认自己是蓝衣社特别服务队的成员，并与该组织的另外四人共同参与了谋杀。
D.B.R.
11月13日。
J. Coyne.
高级警司 (D. S. I.)。

File No. 7595
S.2, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date November 11, 1936.
Subject The Assassination of Gen. Yang Yung Tai, Governor of Hupeh.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne

General Yang Yung Tai (楊永泰), the Governor
of Hupeh Province, was assassinated at Hankow on October
26, 1936, and although a number of persons, including the
assassin, have been apprehended in connection with the crime,
so far the motive has not been made clear.
General Yang, a man of high scholastic attainment,
was at one time the secretary of Gen. Chiang Kai Shek, by
whom he was held in high regard. As a close personal friend
of the Generalissimo he was frequently called upon for
opinions pertaining to internal political affairs, and was
responsible for the preparation of many of the manifestoes
and circular telegrams which emanated from Nanking.
Before his promotion to the Governorship of
Hupeh Gen. Yang held the appointment of Quarter-master
to the Forces, the only military post he ever held.
In some quarters it is believed that the assas-
sination was instigated by members of the old South West
Clique who believed that their downfall was brought about
by Gen. Yang. That such persons are the culprits is possible,
although it is doubtful whether for the reason mentioned.
The collapse of Gen. Chen Chi Tang was brought about by Gen. Tau
（印：RECD 12 NOV 1936 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
Lai Sz, the Governor of Kiangsu Province, under whom Gen.
Chiang Kai Shek served as Chief of Staff before the days
of the Northern Expedition.
At present it is difficult to say which party
might have been responsible for the crime, as any of the
several cliques whose plans have recently been thwarted by
the Generalissimo may have considered that Gen. Yang had
contributed to their embarrassment.
S.Q.
D.C. (Special Branch).
D.S.I.

特务科第2股。

日期 1936年11月11日。
主题 湖北省主席杨永泰将军遇刺案。
撰写人及转呈人：警司 Coyne

湖北省主席杨永泰将军 (Yang Yung Tai) 于1936年10月26日在汉口遇刺，尽管包括刺客在内的多名相关人员已被捕，但动机至今尚未明朗。
杨将军学识渊博，曾任蒋介石将军的秘书，深受蒋的器重。作为委员长的亲密私人朋友，他经常就被征询有关内部政治事务的意见，并负责起草许多从南京发出的宣言和通电。
在升任湖北省主席之前，杨将军担任军需总监，这是他所担任过的唯一军事职务。
在某些方面，人们认为此次刺杀是由西南旧系成员煽动的，他们认为自己的垮台是由杨将军造成的。这些人可能是罪魁祸首，但是否出于上述原因则值得怀疑。陈济棠将军的垮台是由江苏省主席陶来思将军 (Gen. Tau Lai Sz) 促成的，在北伐之前，蒋介石将军曾在其麾下担任参谋长。
目前很难说哪一方可能对罪行负责，因为近期计划被委员长挫败的几个派系中的任何一个都可能认为杨将军导致了他们的尴尬处境。
S.Q.
特务科副警务总监 (D.C.)。
高级警司 (D.S.I.)。
（印：1936年11月12日收到 RECD 12 NOV 1936 上海公共租界工部局警务处）

Date November 10, 1936.
Subject Return of Warrants to Shanghai Special District Court
for Cancellation.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne

Forwarded herewith for cancellation by the Shanghai
First Special Area District Court are four warrants issued
at the request of the Woosung and Shanghai Garrison Com-
mander's Headquarters on November 3, 1936.
No attempt was made to execute Warrant No.588 for the
arrest of Zau Siau Tshing, or Warrant No.589 for the search
of his quarters at No.52 Tah Li Hong, Bubbling Well Road,
as the Chief Detective of the Garrison Commander's Office
stated that the wanted man was no longer residing at that
address.
（批：All Warrants returned to Court 10/11）
Regarding Warrant No.586 for the arrest of Nyi Sz
(倪氏), wife of Yang Er Chi (杨尔赤) and Warrant No.587
for the search of her home at No.34 Oong Yoen Faung, Wei-
haiwei Road, when this address was visited at 7.30 p.m.
November 3, it was ascertained from other occupants of the
house that the wanted person had been absent since noon the
previous day.
No search was made of the premises but detectives
were left in the alleyway to watch the house. As neither
the wanted woman or any of her relatives visited the
premises the watch was withdrawn on November 6 at the
request of the Garrison Commander's Office.

（批：D.B.C. 10/11）
J Coyne
D. S. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 10 NOV. 1936）

CHINESE ADVICE TO JAPANESE RESIDENTS IN SHANGHAI
The other day the Chinese
First District Citizens Federation issued a letter of
advice to Japanese residents in Shanghai advocating
co-operation between Japanese and Chinese. Of course
Japanese have always been devoting themselves to this
end. The letter also refers to the activities of our
naval landing party in Shanghai.
We are discouraged to find that
the letter of the Chinese Citizens Federation is based
on prejudice. People often talk about the result but
over-look the cause. It will be better for them to
ask themselves whether Japanese residents are being
adequately protected by the Chinese authorities; to
reflect upon the various incidents that have taken place
one after the other. It is a fact that during the
past ten years the lives and property of Japanese have
been continuously threatened and at times the situation
has brought in foreign troops including Japanese soldiers
to Shanghai. It is to be hoped that the Federation
will devote itself to improving the relations between
the two countries. The letter also deals with political
and diplomatic affairs and is an attempt to check the
activities of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party.
We would request the Federation to reflect over the
cause for such action. It would be better for them to
cease all anti-Japanese activities first and attempt to
promote Sino-Japanese relations afterwards. Robbers
fear policemen, while good citizens are thankful to the
Police. Chinese people fear marines. We wonder why.

November 4, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE HWA LIEN NEWS AGENCY

The Hwa Lien News Agency (華聯通信社)
was established four years ago. As a certain nation dislikes
this agency, the latter rented a Post Office box as a
communication address. The last Chief of the agency was
a man named Zia Kwang/Nan (謝南光). He was arrested at
Amoy by officials of a certain nation in July this year
when he was on his way to Shanghai from Hongkong. It is
said that the tendons of his leg were removed. His
whereabouts are unknown. The present Chief of the agency is
a man named Yueh Chien Chung (郁建中), native of Tai Chong,
age 31, living at House 30, Lane 280, Rue Chapsal, French
Concession.

At 4 a.m. November 3 a certain organ
requested assistance from the French Police to arrest
Yueh and others in connection with certain activities. At
7 a.m. M. Sarly, Chief of the Political Section, detailed
a large number of detectives and policemen to the address
in Rue Chapel. Yueh Chien Chung, the Chief of the agency,
Woo Chang Chih (吳世植) alias Woo Chang Tse (吳世澤),
a radio operator, and a clerk named Wu (胡), who were
having breakfast at the time, were placed under arrest.
No documents were found on the premises.

A reporter of this paper learns that
Woo is a Korean and a certain nation has been trying to
arrest him for a long time. The three arrested persons
are being detained by the French Police and are being
fairly well treated. The office of the agency has been
occupied by detectives. The affairs of the agency have
been practically suspended and no reports were distributed
last night.

China Times :-

Yueh Chien Chung was a student of the
Nan Fong College (南方大學). He took over the Hwa Lien
News Agency in June, 1935. Wang Chien Chiu (王劍秋), a
native of Fukien, is the editor-in-chief, Woo Chang Shih
(吳昌世), a native of Taiwan, is the radio operator, and
a man named Fong (方), native of Taiwan, is a clerk. The
agency also employs a tea-boy named Li Shih Shing (李世鑫).
Woo Cheng Shih was brought up in Japan
and speaks the Japanese language fluently. Every day he
takes down political, social and financial news sent by
radio from Tokyo, Kobe and Osaka and from the North-east.
Woo also undertakes the translation of Japanese newspapers
and magazines and copies are distributed among the various
local newspapers for publication. The agency is quite
well known locally. It has no branches, but has special
correspondents in Peiping, Tientsin, Hongkong, Amoy and
other places. The agency makes a monthly income of $300
through news supplied to the newspapers as well as other
sources of revenue. Its expenses amount to $600 or $700
a month.

华联新闻社

华联新闻社（華聯通信社）

在厦门被某国官员逮捕。据说他的腿筋被挑断。其
下落不明。该社现任社长是

31岁，居住于法租界卡斯帕尔路（Rue Chapsal）280弄30号。

11月3日凌晨4时，某机关
请求法国警察协助逮捕郁某及其他涉及某些活动的人员。上午7时，政治部主任萨利（Sarly）先生派遣大量侦探和警察前往卡斯帕尔路（Rue Chapel，原文如此，应为Chapsal）的地址。当时正在吃早餐的该社社长郁建中、无线电操作员吴世植（Woo Chang Chih），别名吴世泽（Woo Chang Tse），以及一名姓胡（Wu）的职员，均被逮捕。在该处所未发现任何文件。

本报记者从可靠渠道获悉，
吴氏是朝鲜人，某国长期试图逮捕他。三名被捕人员
正由法国警察拘留，待遇相当不错。该社办公室已被侦探占据。该社事务实际上已暂停，昨晚未分发任何报道。

《字林西报》（China Times）：

Subject: Raids made at the request of the Chinese authorities
         following the assassination of General YANG YUNG TAI.

Reference: Assassination of General YANG YUNG TAI.
           -------

At 9 a.m. November 2, 1936 Inspector YANG VONG GHI of the
Crime Branch of the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander's HQS
came to our office and made the following statement:

"Following the assassination of General Yang Yung Tai
"(杨永泰), governor of Hupeh, the Hankow authorities,
"besides arresting the murderer named CHEN HSUSH CHAO
"(陈受朝), apprehended a certain number of individuals
"implicated in different ways in this case. Among these
"is one YANG CHI SING (杨其新), who has denounced the
"instigators of the crime, and who was brought to Shanghai
"in order to permit the continuing of investigations.
"YANG CHI SING, who was lengthily interrogated by us
"formally denounced a certain YANG EUL TCHE (杨尔济)
"alias PAH KOU (白口), who was living at No. 3
"Delastre Terrace (Passage 109), Route Delastre. We ask
"you to have this man arrested so that he may be extradited
"to the Chinese Authorities."

The necessary assistance was immediately afforded Inspector
YANG VONG GHI, but the raid which was made upon the above mentioned
address, although confirming that YANG EUL TCHE had been residing
at this place, did not allow us to effect his arrest; the house
was shut up and empty.

Later during the morning, a watch maintained by us over the
premises permitted us to identify certain of its residents.

At 10.30 a.m. there was NI TEH SHENG (倪得胜); who carried
a key of the house and a basket full of groceries. He claimed to
know nothing of his master whom he had never seen and did not even
know his name. Still later he admitted, after he had been
"caught" telling lies, that he was the father-in-law of YANG EUL
TCHE. At the request of the Chinese Authorities he was kept
under watch being arrested at 5 p.m. November 3. He will appear
before Court on November 4 (Extradition proceedings).

At 12.15 p.m. a young man of 16, named LI CHING KI (李群坚),
adopted son of YANG EUL TCHI, returned to the premises from the
Chung-Kuo School (中國), Route de Sieyes.

Under interrogation this youth admitted that he had made a
trip to Hankow from October 21 until November 1, but that he was not

主题：应中国当局请求，在杨永泰将军遇刺案后进行的搜查行动。

参考：杨永泰将军遇刺案。
-------

1936年11月2日上午9时，吴淞-上海警备司令部稽查处督察杨荣基（YANG VONG GHI，音译）来到本局办公室，并作如下陈述：

“继湖北省主席杨永泰将军遇刺后，汉口当局除逮捕名为陈受朝（CHEN HSUSH CHAO）的凶手外，还抓获了若干以不同方式卷入此案的人员。其中有一人杨其新（YANG CHI SING），他揭发了犯罪的指使者，并被带至上海以便继续进行调查。经我方长时间讯问，杨其新正式指控一名叫杨尔济（YANG EUL TCHE，音译）、别名白口（PAH KOU，音译）的人，此人居住于德拉司特路（Route Delastre）德拉司特里弄（Passage 109）3号。请贵方逮捕此人，以便将其引渡给中国当局。”

我局立即向杨荣基督察提供了必要的协助，但对上述地址进行的搜查虽证实杨尔济曾居住于此，却未能将其逮捕；该房屋门窗紧闭，内无一人。

随后在当天上午，我局对该处所实施的监视使我们得以辨认出其中的某些居住者。

上午10时30分，倪得胜（NI TEH SHENG）出现；他携带着该房屋的钥匙和一篮食品杂货。他声称对自己的主人一无所知，从未见过面，甚至不知道其姓名。后来在被“当场抓获”说谎后，他承认自己是杨尔济的岳父。应中国当局请求，对其实施监视，并于11月3日下午5时将其逮捕。他将于11月4日出庭（引渡程序）。

中午12时15分，一名16岁的青年李群坚（LI CHING KI），系杨尔济（YANG EUL TCHI，音译）的养子，从西爱咸斯路（Route de Sieyes）的中国学校（Chung-Kuo School，中國）返回该处所。

经讯问，这名青年承认他于10月21日至11月1日期间前往汉口，但他并非

page_data.en:
2
in the capital of Hupeh on the day of the assasination of General
Yang - October 25 - having in the meantime been to Canton to obtain
some money that his adopted father had been unable to give him.
He says that the trip to Hankow had as its sole object the finding
of his father-in-law in order to ask him for some money for the
"family." In his statement he confirms that YANG SUL TCHE was
in Hankow at the time that the crime was committed.
The young LI CHING KI was arrested at 5 p.m. November 3, at the
request of the Chinese Authorities. He will appear before the
Court on November 4 together with NI TEH SENG.
------
Meanwhile, during the night of November 2/3, representatives
of the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander's HQS had further inter-
rogated the prisoner from Hankow YANG CHI SING. Through him they
learnt that another individual had played an important role in the
organisation of the assassination. It concerned one YUEH CHI TSONG
(郁建中), director of the Hwa-Lien (華聯) Press Agency.
At 10 a.m. November 4, Inspector YANG VONG GHI, having secured the
necessary information, presented himself at our office and requested
that we arrest YUEH CHI TSONG with a view to extradition. The
assistance requested was immediately afforded him. At No. 3,
passage No. 280, rue Chapsal, where we made our way to conduct the
raid, we discovered the secret Hwa-Lien Press Agency. This
agency which had removed from the Concession to the Settlement in
August 1935 after an abortive raid made by us on July 29, 1935 at
10/160 avenue Dubail on the authority of a warrant issued by the
Second District Court at the request of the Bureau of Public
Safety, returned to the Concession during September 1936. YUEH
CHI TSONG was immediately placed under arrest as was one of his friends
named LI YONG TSONG (李用中). Both of them will be brought
before Court on November 4 with a view to extraditing them. A
Korean CHANG SEI O (Korean pronunciation) or WU CHANG SE (Chinese
pronunciation)(吳昌世) was the only member of the staff of the
agency who took up our attention and that of the Chinese Authorities
apart from the above two mentioned individuals. His duties comprised
the translating for YUEH CHI TSONG news sent out in Japanese by
Japanese radio stations. After interrogation he was handed over
page_data.zh:
2
在杨将军遇刺当日——10月25日——身处湖北省会，在此期间他去了广州，去取他的养父无法给他的钱。他说，去汉口的唯一目的是寻找他的岳父，以便为“家庭”向他讨要一些钱。在他的供词中，他证实案发时杨尔济（YANG SUL TCHE，音译）身在汉口。
应中国当局请求，青年李群坚于11月3日下午5时被逮捕。他将与倪得胜于11月4日一同出庭。
------
与此同时，在11月2日至3日的夜间，吴淞-上海警备司令部的代表进一步讯问了来自汉口的囚犯杨其新。通过他，他们获悉另一人在组织刺杀行动中发挥了重要作用。此人是郁建中（YUEH CHI TSONG），华联（Hwa-Lien，華聯）通讯社社长。
11月4日上午10时，杨荣基督察在获取必要信息后，来到本局办公室，请求逮捕郁建中以备引渡。我局立即向其提供了所请求的协助。在霞飞路（rue Chapsal）280弄3号，我们前往执行搜查行动，发现了秘密的华联通讯社。该通讯社曾在1935年7月29日我局根据第二特区法院应公安局请求签发的搜查令，对都百里路（avenue Dubail）10/160号进行一次未成功的搜查后，于1935年8月从法租界迁至公共租界，后又于1936年9月返回法租界。郁建中及其一名名叫李用中（LI YONG TSONG）的朋友随即被捕。两人均将于11月4日被带上法庭，以备引渡。除上述两人外，一名朝鲜人张世五（CHANG SEI O，朝鲜语发音）或吴昌世（WU CHANG SE，中文发音）（吳昌世）是该通讯社职员中唯一引起我局及中国当局注意的人。他的职责是为郁建中翻译日本电台发出的日语新闻。经讯问后，他于

page_data.en:
3
to the Japanese Authorities at 5 p.m. November 3. At first sight
he does not appear compromised in the murder of General YANG YUNG
TAI.
evidence
Although the charges against the four prisoners at the
moment does not seem to be overwhelming, it appears however sufficient
to justify their extradition.
NI TEH SENG ( 倪德陞 ), lied to us in trying to pass himself off as
a servant and stating that he had never seen YANG EUL
TCHE, since the latter is a relative, and further he
passed the nights of the 1st. and 2nd. at 3/180 route
Delastre. Documents and rooms examined at 3/180
route Delastre only go to support the presumptions
arising from his attitude.
LI CHING KI ( 李群堅 ), is an important suspect. His trip to Hankow
and Canton (by the Hankow-Canton Railway) make one
believe that he was charged with the fulfilling of a
liaison mission between certain terrorist organisations
having their headquarters in South China and YANG EUL
TCHE who was in Hankow at the time of the assassination
of General Yang Yung Tai.
YUEH CHI TSONG ( 俞建中 ), as director of the Hwa-Lien Agency, is
also a suspect. He is formally accused by the prisoner
CHEN HSUEH CHAO ( 盛學超 ), and among the many letters
found on him, one was discovered bearing the name of
YANG EUL TCHE.
LI YONG TSONG ( 李用中 ), as a friend of the foregoing person, is
also a suspect. A document found on him with the
address of YANG EUL TCHE (which he endeavoured to
dispose of) indicates that he was on the point of leaving
Shanghai with an "unknown" who would have been able to
identify himself as YANG EUL TCHE.
Up to the present none of the four individuals arrested
acknowledge having participated directly or indirectly in the
preparation for the attack on General Yang Yung Tai. None object
to being handed over to the Chinese Authorities, to whom they state
they can prove their innocence. Only LI YUNG TSONG requests that
proof of his guilt be produced by the Chinese Authorities.
page_data.zh:
3
11月3日下午5时被移交给日本当局。乍看之下，他似乎并未卷入杨永泰将军谋杀案。
证据
虽然目前针对这四名囚犯的指控似乎并不确凿，但看来足以证明将其引渡是正当的。
倪德陞（NI TEH SENG，原文拼写为Seng，前文为Sheng），试图冒充仆人并谎称从未见过杨尔济，以此欺骗我们，鉴于后者是其亲属，且他于1日和2日晚住在德拉司特路180弄3号。在德拉司特路180弄3号检查的文件和房间仅佐证了由其态度产生的推测。
李群坚（LI CHING KI），是一名重要嫌疑人。他的汉口和广州之行（经由粤汉铁路）使人相信，他受命在中国南方某些恐怖组织总部与案发时在汉口的杨尔济之间履行联络任务。
俞建中（YUEH CHI TSONG，此处中文名译为俞建中，前文为郁建中），作为华联社社长，也是一名嫌疑人。他被囚犯盛学超（CHEN HSUEH CHAO，原文拼音为Chen，中文名为盛）正式指控，在他身上发现的多封信件中，有一封署有杨尔济的名字。
李用中（LI YONG TSONG），作为上述人员的友人，也是一名嫌疑人。在他身上发现的一份载有杨尔济地址的文件（他试图销毁该文件）表明，他正准备与一名“身份不明者”离开上海，而此人本可表明自己就是杨尔济。
截至目前，四名被捕者中无人承认直接或间接参与了对杨永泰将军袭击行动的筹备工作。无人反对被移交给中国当局，他们表示可以向中国当局证明自己的清白。只有李用中要求中国当局出示其有罪的证据。

November 4, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE HWA LIEN NEWS AGENCY

The Hwa Lien News Agency (華聯通信社)
was established four years ago. As a certain nation dislikes
this agency, the latter rented a Post Office box as a
communication address. The last Chief of the agency was
a man named Zia Kwang/Nan (謝南光). He was arrested at
Amoy by officials of a certain nation in July this year
when he was on his way to Shanghai from Hongkong. It is
said that the tendons of his leg were removed. His
whereabouts are unknown. The present Chief of the agency is
a man named Yueh Chien Chung (郁建中), native of Tai Chong,
age 31, living at House 30, Lane 280, Rue Chapsal, French
Concession.
At 4 a.m. November 3 a certain organ
requested assistance from the French Police to arrest
Yueh and others in connection with certain activities. At
7 a.m. M. Sarly, Chief of the Political Section, detailed
a large number of detectives and policemen to the address
in Rue Chapsal. Yueh Chien Chung, the Chief of the agency,
Woo Chang Chih (吳世植) alias Woo Chang Tse (吳世澤),
a radio operator, and a clerk named Wu (胡), who were
having breakfast at the time, were placed under arrest.
No documents were found on the premises.
A reporter of this paper learns that
Woo is a Korean and a certain nation has been trying to
arrest him for a long time. The three arrested persons
are being detained by the French Police and are being
fairly well treated. The office of the agency has been
occupied by detectives. The affairs of the agency have
been practically suspended and no reports were distributed
last night.

China Times :-

Yueh Chien Chung was a student of the
Nan Fong College (南方大學). He took over the Hwa Lien
News Agency in June, 1935. Wang Chien Chiu (王劍秋), a
native of Fukien, is the editor-in-chief, Woo Chang Shih
(吳昌世), a native of Taiwan, is the radio operator, and
a man named Fong (方), native of Taiwan, is a clerk. The
agency also employs a tea-boy named Li Shih Shing (李世鑫).
Woo Chang Shih was brought up in Japan
and speaks the Japanese language fluently. Every day he
takes down political, social and financial news sent by
radio from Tokyo, Kobe and Osaka and from the North-east.
Woo also undertakes the translation of Japanese newspapers
and magazines and copies are distributed among the various
local newspapers for publication. The agency is quite
well known locally. It has no branches, but has special
correspondents in Peiping, Tientsin, Hongkong, Amoy and
other places. The agency makes a monthly income of $300
through news supplied to the newspapers as well as other
sources of revenue. Its expenses amount to $600 or $700
a month.

11月3日凌晨4时，某机关请求法国警察协助逮捕郁某等人，涉及某些活动。上午7时，政治部主任萨利先生（M. Sarly）派遣大量侦探和警察前往霞飞路的地址。当时正在吃早餐的通讯社社长郁建中、无线电操作员吴世植（Woo Chang Chih，吳世植），别名吴世泽（Woo Chang Tse，吳世澤），以及一名姓胡（Wu，此处英文为Wu，中文注为胡）的职员，均被逮捕。在该处所未发现任何文件。
